title: The Human Cardiovascular System
text: The cardiovascular (circulatory) system consists of the heart, blood vessels (arteries, veins, capillaries), and blood. The heart is a muscular pump that drives blood through approximately 60,000 miles (96,000 km) of blood vessels. The heart's four chambers — two atria and two ventricles — pump blood through two circuits: the pulmonary circulation (right side, to the lungs for oxygenation) and the systemic circulation (left side, to the rest of the body). The heart beats approximately 100,000 times per day. Blood pressure is the force exerted by blood against vessel walls; normal is about 120/80 mmHg. Cardiovascular diseases — including coronary artery disease, heart failure, and stroke — are the leading cause of death globally.
